title: XRF Calibration for Quantification of Inorganic Elements in Lipsticks
author: Pilakouta, Trapali, et al.
materials: The selected elements cover a region of Kα energies from 3.3 to 29 KeV corresponding to elements potassium (K) to iodine (I). Furthermore, heavier elements were also prepared for using Lα lines.

steps.title: Prepare calibration stock solutions
steps.instruction: Dissolve the compounds listed in Table 1a (K, Fe, Cu, Br, Sn, I, Pb) in water to make solutions at concentrations ranging from 0.5 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ to 5 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹; prepare 0.17 M citric‑acid solutions of Ga, Sb, La, Mo and Ba and dilute them with water to the same final concentration range; use the masses given in Table 1a (e.g., 93.3 g KI, 66.4 g FeCl₃, 48.0 g Cu(NO₃)₂·3H₂O, etc.) to calculate the required volumes; note that KBr and KI are treated specially and are not used for a single element Homa.

steps.title: Deposit calibration droplets on thin film
steps.instruction: Using a micropipette, place 40 µL–700 µL of each calibration solution onto a Prolene 4.0 µm thin‑film support mounted in a double‑open‑ended sample cup; for optimal droplet‑trace diameter, use volumes between 200 µL and 500 µL, which produce dried traces 0.7–1.5 cm in diameter (area 0.38–2.5 cm²), larger than the X‑ray beam spot (~0.4 cm diameter with a 2 mm collimator).

steps.title: Dry droplets and check trace size
steps.instruction: Allow the droplets to dry physically for at least 24 h; verify that the dried trace diameter exceeds the beam spot (≥0.4 cm) before proceeding.

steps.title: Assess homogeneity of each Homa
steps.instruction: For every element and concentration, prepare at least three Homas; first inspect each dried Homa visually for uniform appearance; then measure XRF yield at two or three random positions on the same Homa; accept a Homa only if the variation among positions is within the statistical uncertainty and does not exceed 10 %; record the average yield as the Homa’s yield.

steps.title: Estimate surface density of Homas
steps.instruction: Calculate the mass of the target element in each droplet (mass = solution concentration × volume used); divide this mass by the measured droplet‑trace area to obtain surface density (µg cm⁻²); the overall accuracy of the thin Homas is about 15 % due to homogeneity and surface‑density uncertainties.

steps.title: Acquire XRF spectra of standards and blank
steps.instruction: Collect XRF spectra for each accepted Homa and for a blank (empty membrane) using the same instrumental settings; spectra may be analyzed with any suitable software (e.g., Amptek DppMCA or SPECTRW).

steps.title: Calculate elemental sensitivity factors
steps.instruction: For each element, use at least three Homas of different concentrations plus the blank; plot XRF yield (cps) versus surface density (µg cm⁻²) and perform linear regression; the slope gives the sensitivity factor SFi in units of cps·µg⁻¹·cm² (or cps·mg⁻¹·cm² as reported).

steps.title: Generate overall sensitivity calibration curve
steps.instruction: Combine the sensitivity factors obtained from all elements (K, Fe, Cu, Ga, Br, I, Sb, Pb, etc.) and fit the data with a second‑order polynomial over the 3–14 keV energy range (Fig. 6); this curve can be used to estimate sensitivity factors for elements not directly measured.

steps.title: Estimate SFs for additional elements
steps.instruction: Apply the polynomial fit to calculate sensitivity factors for other elements (e.g., Ti, Rb, Sr, Zr) as shown in Table 3; note that the potassium SF was taken as the mean of the KBr and KI Homas.

steps.title: Compare with commercial standards (optional)
steps.instruction: For Cu, Ga, Br, Sb and Pb, compare the Homa‑derived SFs with those obtained from commercial micromatter standards (Table 2); reported differences range from 6 % to 20 %.

steps.title: Prepare and analyse unknown samples
steps.instruction: Prepare test samples (lipsticks, creams, toothpastes) on the same Prolene film, let them dry physically for at least 24 h, and analyse them by XRF using the calibrated sensitivity factors to quantify elemental concentrations.

steps.title: Record unsuccessful Homa attempts
steps.instruction: Note that attempts to prepare homogeneous Homas for Ti, Ni, Zn, Mo, Sn, Ba and La were unsuccessful due to homogeneity problems; these elements are therefore excluded from the calibration set.
